citation: Harold Allen for HABS, 'View: exterior - from NW, north (18th St.) and west (Prairie Ave.) elevations', W. W. Kimball House, 1801 South Prairie Avenue, Chicago, June 1965. HABS IL-1077 photograph 2 of 3 (call number HABS ILL,16-CHIG,75--2). Library of Congress.
author: Harold Allen (HABS)
repository: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division (HABS). Master TIFF 580873pu.tif (5275 x 3996 px, sha256 a51fa2b30ddae5b43cf228bee49a601f21eb896ca18cad50b4351f78c4a87b58); 1800 px web copy committed at chicago/prairie_1904_v1/research/public/kimball-habs-photo-02.jpg (Prairie library a18-kimball-habs-photo-02).
locator: The whole plate, from the north-west corner of Prairie Avenue and 18th Street: the front's north end with the loggia, its bowed bay and the south pavilion's gable foreshortened at the right, and the whole 18th Street flank running east to the alley: the round tower, the flank section, the gabled section with its oriel, the east range under its slate roof and wall dormers, and the north-east turret.
rights_note: Made for HABS (U.S. Government); LOC: no known restrictions. Measurements only; nothing derived as an asset.
access_notes: Read 2026-10-26 (T-3110) from the LOC master TIFF, reduced to 1800 px; camera solved in data/reference_views/kimball_house_1801_prairie/habs_1965_02_northwest.json. The copy is not mirrored: the plate's own 'HABS No. ILL-1077' reads true along its left edge (written sideways) and the flank runs east to the left of the corner, as it must from the north-west.
note: A 1965 photograph: evidence of the house as it stood that June, carried to 1904 only for fabric the Taylor photograph of c. 1895 or the 1911 sheet does not contradict (the house was built 1890-92 and the survey describes its exterior as substantially as built). It is the only picture known to this project that shows the 18th Street flank's east range whole: in the Taylor print a tree stands in front of it.
what_it_supplies: the east range's north face whole, from the gabled section to the north-east turret: its wall height, its slate roof and its stone wall dormers, its door and its openings, through the solved camera
a second camera on the 18th Street flank and the front's north end, to check the Taylor print's readings
what_it_does_not_supply: the 1904 state of anything altered between 1904 and 1965 (the window air-conditioners are 1960s; the fence and the street furniture are not read)
the rear (east) wall or the court side: the camera cannot see them
